newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt allocations remain defensive-survey.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt allocations remain defensive-survey.

text.p: Money managers' U.S. debt portfolios saw very little change in the week ended September 17, said a survey by Stone & McCarthy Research Associates Inc.
"There wasn't a lot going on in this week's survey," the report said, noting that "the measures of duration exposure remain near the most defensive since early August."
The report said the survey's bear/bull index arithmetic reading fell to 4.00 from 4.14 the week before, while the asset-weighted number came in at 4.18, up from the 4.08 in the previous period.
A number above 5.00 is seen as indicating investors are mostly long on the market.
The cash/assets ratio fell to 7.21 percent from 7.31 percent.
Duration bogey held steady at 4.06 on an arithmetic basis and 4.69 on a weighted basis.
Duration bogey is the level of asset or liability duration sought in the management of a portfolio.
Duration refers to a portfolio's average maturity and is used by portfolio managers to calculate exposure to risk.

Four percent of the portfolio managers polled said they were planning to be active in the coming week, up from nil the week before. The bear/bull index collected among those who intend to be active was 4.00; last week the number was not available.
The Stone & McCarthy survey is conducted by the research firm weekly. It includes 25 market participants with total assets of about $100 billion, the firm said.
* Table provided by Stone and McCarthy Research Associates.
** Respondents intending to adjust portfolio in coming week.
